publicReleaseNotes: Uptime 0.5.11 makes maintenance plans and monitor erasure receipts easier to read: selected monitors are named, erasure explains what was removed, and the receipt reference can be copied. Exact per-table counts and the original receipt ID remain under Receipt details and in the downloadable receipt. Heartbeat summaries show the saved cron expression, time zone, grace and maximum run duration, or the period plus grace. Scheduled health evaluation follows the saved job's deadline and duration limit instead of also applying an unrelated period age limit; older receipts without a job snapshot cannot establish cron health. A private runner is still required, and only signed scheduled checks change health. Development and demo invitations now explain that no email was sent and how to choose the invited account. Local sign-in guidance points to the private RER_OPEN link printed by rer dev; keep it private because it gives access to the local installation. Hosted invitation delivery is unchanged. No migration or new required settings; monitors, history, incidents, destinations and private settings are kept on upgrade. The pinned @runeditrun/rer stays at 0.2.108; update an existing checkout with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile. Archive transfer bounds and unestablished capacity remain as described in 0.5.10; bounded-memory restore, operation at 500 monitors with 90 days of history, time-range selection and console chunk-transfer controls are not established or remain unavailable. Known issues: heartbeat output saved by 0.5.6 or earlier is not rewritten, so rotate a key earlier output may have contained; pattern-based redaction can still miss an unlabelled secret of no recognizable shape that is not listed under Output text to mask. A monitor CSV exported from UptimeRobot still cannot be imported. Restoring an archive does not restore the list of erased people, so pairing again with a Business that still lists them could invite them again. A company with a signed agent policy but no company settings receives an empty decision feed rather than a refusal. Response bodies over 64 KiB still fail the check; monitor a smaller health endpoint. Other earlier release limits remain. The product screenshot was taken on 0.4.0, before the console changes of 0.5.0 through 0.5.11. Product screenshot: .github/assets/release/uptime-0.4.0-monitor-1440.png
